text:
tanvi: Heads-up — I noticed the p99 on the latency dashboard for /v2/complete jumps ~30ms when I toggle the histogram overlay between endpoints :eyes:
seb: Which dashboard? link? :point_up:
seb: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/route-latency-compare (the one with endpoint breakdown)
tanvi: That one. If I overlay per-endpoint histograms the p50/p95/p99 lines shift compared to the standalone percentile series. Screenshot omitted, but the p99 moves up when histogram overlay is on.
maria: Short answer: not a rendering bug, usually an aggregation-source mismatch. The percentile series is from TDigest rollups, the histogram overlay comes from bucketed histograms that the UI rebins and smooths differently.
dave: Two quick hypotheses: 1) the histogram layer applies a sliding smoothing kernel in the UI, 2) the percentile series is computed from a different aggregation window or sample-origin subset (edge vs backend). Could be clock skew too.
tanvi: Can paste the query I used for the percentile?
tanvi: ```
SELECT percentile(0.99) as p99 FROM latency_samples
WHERE route = '/v2/complete' AND timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY endpoint
ORDER BY timestamp ASC
```
maria: That query is fine. The console, when you enable histogram overlay, does an additional re-aggregation for histograms with default binning and a 30s smoothing window. Re-aggregating buckets -> slightly different quantiles than TDigest rollup.
observability-bot: note: rollout meta: A/B cohort merge enabled for route /v2/complete since 2026-03-10; sample_origin tag present (client|edge|backend).
seb: UX idea: expose 'percentile source' in the widget (rollup vs histogram-derived) and show a small badge like "computed from histograms" when that's the case. That would avoid surprise.
dan: (typo, ignore)
dave: Quick mitigation: add an on-widget annotation that reads "histogram overlay may use different aggregation and smoothing; toggle raw samples for parity". I can drive a tiny ticket for the UI and a backend flag to surface percentile_source.
maria: I'll also add a docs blurb explaining how smoothing windows and binning affect quantiles and when to expect divergence.
seb: Also add an optional debug view that shows sample counts per bucket/time-slice, that helped in past incidents.
tanvi: Sounds good. Can you file the UX ticket @dave and a docs PR @maria? I'll attach the trace and a reproducible screenshot when I get back to my laptop. Thanks :thumbsup:
dave: Filed ENGPLT-1429 "Expose percentile_source and histogram parity toggle"; assigned to frontend infra + eng-platform.
maria: I'll draft the docs PR and ping for review.
tanvi: Great, thanks. If we want a backwards-compatible quick fix we could also default histogram overlay to "no smoothing" but warn about higher noise. I'll try that locally tomorrow and report back.
seb: Nice. Keep an eye on sample_origin splits — if one endpoint mostly backend samples, that alone can change p99.
tanvi: Will do. Closing for now, will re-open if I can reproduce without the overlay. :eyes:
